topic: Mantis shrimp: punch force, cavitation, color vision, club armor
hook: A shrimp that punches 2,500x its body weight
caption:
A mantis shrimp's punch can hit with forces over 2,500 times its own body weight, and it's fast enough to make the water itself strike its prey a second time.

The twist: with 12 color receptors to our 3, you'd expect super color vision. Experiments found they're actually worse than us at telling close colors apart. (Sources: Patek et al., Nature 2004; Thoen et al., Science 2014)

1/5 Faster than a blink (23 m/s)
Its club-like arm strikes at up to 23 meters per second, finishing in just a few milliseconds.
📷 Alexander Vasenin (CC BY-SA 3.0) via wikimedia

2/5 Two hits in one (2x)
The strike is so fast it creates collapsing bubbles in the water, hitting the prey a second time.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/5 12 color receptors (12)
Humans see color with 3 types of cones. Mantis shrimp have 12 types of color receptors.
📷 Cédric Peneau (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 But worse at color (Twist)
Tests show they tell similar colors apart worse than we do. They likely recognize colors fast, not finely.
📷 Cédric Peneau (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

5/5 Armor engineers copy
Its club has a spiral fiber structure that stops cracks. Scientists study it to design tougher materials.
📷 Diego Delso (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia
